**<mark>ICSG PRESS RELEASE Date Issued: 21</mark>**<sup>**st**</sup> **<mark>October 2010</mark>** 



# **Copper: Preliminary Data for July 2010** 

The International Copper Study Group (ICSG) released preliminary data for July 2010 world copper supply and demand in its October 2010 Copper Bulletin. The Bulletin is available for sale upon request. 

According to preliminary ICSG data, the refined copper market balance for July 2010 indicated a production deficit of about 50,000 metric tonnes (t). When making seasonal adjustments for world refined production and usage, July showed a deficit of about 25,000 t. The apparent refined copper balance for the first seven month of 2010, including revisions to data previously presented, indicates a production deficit of 356,000 t (a seasonally adjusted deficit of 36,000 t). This compares with a production deficit of around 165,000 t (a seasonally adjusted surplus of about 130,000 t) in the same period of 2009. 

During the seven month of 2010, world apparent usage grew by 7.3% (775,000 t) compared with that in same period of 2009 mainly owing to recovery from weak 2009 usage levels in Japan, the European Union (EU), and the United States, where usage grew by 32%, 12.5%, and 8.3%, respectively.  Combined, these three regions accounted for 32% of total world refined copper usage.  In the same period, Chinese apparent usage* increased by a modest 1.5%, due to the very high apparent usage levels seen in 2009. 

While in July, world mine production increased by 5.8% from that in July 2009, cumulative production for the first 7 months of 2010 increased by a modest 1% (90,000 t) compared with that in the first 7 months of 2009: concentrate and solvent extractionelectrowinning (SX-EW) production both grew by about 1%. Production in Chile was up by 2.4% from its low level during the same period of 2009, but output from, Peru, the United States, Australia and Indonesia decreased by an aggregated 8% (208,000t).  These four countries represent around 25% of total world copper mine production.  The mine capacity utilization rate in the first seven month of 2010 (79.2%) was down slightly from the already low comparative rate in 2009 

During the first seven month of 2010, world refined production increased by 5.6% (580,000 t) compared with production in the same period of 2009: primary production increased by 2.4%, while secondary production (from scrap) increased by 24%. Note that the large relative increase in secondary refined copper production reflects in part the lower copper prices and consequent tight scrap market that existed in early 2009. World growth has been mainly driven by China (16%), Japan (10.6%) and the EU (9.5%) that combined represent almost one half of world refined copper production. Production in two other major world refiners, Chile and the United States, which account for about one quarter of world production, decreased by a combined 2.4%. The refined production capacity utilization rate in the

first seven month of 2010 increased to 79.6% from 76.7% in the same period of 2009 and reflects increased scrap availability and the restoration of temporary cuts made in early 2009. The average LME cash price for September 2010 was US$ 7,709.3 per tonne, up from the August 2010 average of US$ 7,283.95 per tonne. The 2010 high and low copper prices through the end of September were US$8,053.50 and US$6,091.00 per tonne, respectively, and the average was US$7,168.67 per tonne. As of the end of September 2010, copper stocks held at the major metal exchanges (LME, COMEX, SHFE) totalled 537,979 t, a decrease of 149,712 t from stocks held at the end of December 2009. Compared with the August levels, stocks were down at the three exchanges (COMEX, LME and SHFE).
